Funding for better connections in Kaikōura
news.body:
Locals and visitors will benefit from improved access in central Kaikōura, with the Government providing a grant of up to $500,000 from the Regional Infrastructure Fund for new facilities, Regional Development Minister Shane Jones and Tourism Minister Louise Upston say.

Kaikōura District Council will contribute $250,000 towards the $750,000 project, which will improve links between the West End, town centre, visitor facilities and the wider walking and cycling network, including the Whale Trail.

The project comprise a new pedestrian and cycle bridge across Lyell Creek and an extension of the West End car park

“Kaikōura is a tourism success story, and we need to make sure its infrastructure keeps pace. Better access around the town centre will improve the experience for visitors while making it easier for locals to get where they need to go,” Ms Upston says.

“Improving parking and walking and cycling links will make it easier to get around town and help local businesses make the most of the visitors Kaikōura attracts.”

The car park extension is expected to add around 60 spaces, alongside a new access road, footpath and recreational green space. The pedestrian and cycle bridge across Lyell Creek will provide a more direct link between the West End, town centre and wider walking and cycling network.

“This is exactly the sort of targeted regional infrastructure the Regional Infrastructure Fund is designed to support. It meets a practical local need and will make Kaikōura a better-connected place to live, visit and do business,” Mr Jones says.

The project will now progress through detailed design, costing, consenting and procurement before construction can begin.

Milford Tourism concession in place for summer
news.body:
A new concession agreement with Milford Sound Tourism Limited has now been signed – bringing certainty for the iconic tourism destination ahead of summer, Conservation Minister Tama Potaka says.

The concession enables Milford Sound Tourism Limited (MSTL) to continue managing the Piopiotahi Milford Sound visitor terminal and Freshwater Basin carparks through to 2050.

“I’m pleased to announce the completion of this process ensuring the long-term operation of important visitor infrastructure in time to support a predicted record tourism season for Piopiotahi,” says Mr Potaka.

“September cruise boat passenger numbers show an 18% increase so far this financial year compared to last year.”

“Milford Sound Tourism Limited has operated in the area for several decades. It established a shareholder partnership with Ngāi Tahu in 2025 acknowledging the deep cultural significance of Piopiotahi Milford Sound.”

In December 2025 Minister Potaka decided to grant a long-term concession for the operation of key visitor infrastructure at Milford Sound Piopiotahi, subject to terms and conditions being negotiated over the following months.

“Since I made the decision to renew this concession in December last year, DOC has been in discussions with MSTL, Ngāi Tahu, and vessel operators to understand and, where possible, address concerns regarding the operation of the facilities by MSTL.

“Through this engagement DOC developed a set of terms and conditions that are workable and address key matters such as asset management, recognising cultural values, and ensuring robust health and safety and environmental compliance.

“The new concession will provide greater transparency around maintenance and investment plans, to ensure a high-quality visitor experience. It also establishes an operator forum to encourage more proactive and coordinated tourism operations.”

The decision builds on the Government’s wider commitment to conservation and tourism in the Milford corridor, including an $8.2 million investment from the International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy.

“This is an exciting time for tourism to Piopiotahi Milford Sound with a suite of DOC visitor upgrades also on track for summer,” Mr Potaka says.

“These include a new Chasm experience, a new swing bridge and track upgrades at Hinepipiwai Lake Marian Track, and a new recreational boat ramp and toilets at Deepwater Basin.”

Geothermal exploration for Taranaki and Waikato
news.body:
Two Māori-led early exploration projects in Taranaki and South Waikato could unlock new geothermal opportunities beyond New Zealand’s established geothermal areas, supporting regional growth and making greater use of home-grown energy resources, Regional Development and Resources Minister Shane Jones says.

A project exploring low-temperature geothermal resources in Taranaki will receive a $3 million grant from the Regional Infrastructure Fund (RIF), while a further $2.95m grant will be used to explore the South Mangakino geothermal resource in Waikato.

“New Zealand has a long and successful history of geothermal development, primarily concentrated in the Taupō Volcanic Zone and Northland,” Mr Jones says.

“With our geology and world-class expertise, we are exceptionally well placed to make more of geothermal. Exploring more widely in places such as Taranaki and South Waikato will help build a better picture of our geothermal potential and where it could support future regional growth.

The Taranaki Geoheat Demonstrator project, led by Parininihi ki Waitōtara Incorporation, will drill two shallow test wells in the Matemateāonga Formation to improve our understanding of low-temperature geothermal heat and its potential for direct-use applications.

“Unlike the high-temperature resources traditionally associated with geothermal electricity generation, lower-temperature resources could potentially support a range of direct heat uses. Understanding where these resources exist and their characteristics is an important first step towards identifying future development and decarbonisation opportunities,” Mr Jones says.

At South Mangakino, geoscience investigations and a test well led by Wairarapa Moana ki Pouākani Incorporation will explore a geothermal anomaly beneath their Māori freehold land and provide better information about the resource. Any future development will depend on what the exploration finds, alongside further investment and consenting.

“New exploration is only part of the picture. Our From the Ground Up geothermal strategy identified an opportunity to bring data together in one accessible national database. A further $3 million has been set aside from the RIF to progress this work.

“A geothermal database can pull together existing, but fragmented data to support a better understanding of geothermal resources, derisking exploration activity, and supporting development opportunities, promoting regional growth and energy resilience in areas with geothermal resources.

“Together, these initiatives are about more than finding new geothermal resources. They are about helping our regions turn what lies beneath our feet into investment, jobs and long-term economic opportunity.” Mr Jones says.

Wairarapa grain storage set to benefit farmers
news.body:
Wairarapa farmers and allied contractors will reap the benefits of a $1.55 million loan from the Regional Infrastructure Fund to support the establishment of a new grain drying and storage facility in Carterton.

The loan will enable farmers to store up to 4000 tonnes of grain in the region instead of trucking it to Manawatu for storage, Associate Regional Development Minister Mark Patterson says.

The creation of the facility will help support more than 300 workers across farming, transport, contracting and advisory services in the region.

“A large locally based facility will improve costs, efficiencies, and resilience for both grain producers and local farmers who rely on the grain for stock feed.

“Growers have had to store excess grain outside the region, which increases costs and reduces margins for both producers and contractors,.

“This has been compounded by rising diesel prices piling on the costs of transporting grain elsewhere for storage and then back again when needed. This investment restores essential infrastructure and keeps more value in Wairarapa.”

A scalable grain-drying and storage facility is more viable and affordable for Wairarapa growers than the storage, seed-cleaning and processing facilities initially proposed, Mr Patterson says.

“Wairarapa farmers will benefit from a new seed-cleaning and processing facility in central Hawke’s Bay that the Government is also supporting with a $3 million RIF loan.”

The funding is subject to the establishment of a grower-led company to build and run the facility, provision of at least $800,000 of grower equity, and suitable site, delivery, consenting and financial arrangements.

Foxton wetland restoration backed by RIF
news.body:
The restoration and development of Piriharakeke, the river loop at Foxton, will be supported by a grant of up to $3 million from the Regional Infrastructure Fund, Regional Development Minister Shane Jones says.

“Piriharakeke is a waterway of deep significance to local hapū of Ngāti Raukawa and the wider Foxton community," Mr Jones says.

“Historically, Piriharakeke was an important mahinga kai where Māori gathered food and, later, a key transport corridor supporting the Port of Foxton.

“Over the past century, changes to the wider Manawatū River system have contributed to the decline of the river loop, degrading its environmental health and limiting community use.”

Proposed works to enhance the health of Piriharakeke include new walkways, jetties and boardwalks, improved access to the river, native planting, dredging, and other environmental improvements.

“This investment will help restore the health of the river, reconnect people with the awa, and create further opportunities for recreation, tourism and Māori enterprise while building on years of local effort to revitalise this important community asset," Mr Jones says.

The project forms Phase 3 of a broader programme of Crown-supported investment in Foxton's revitalisation over the past 10 years.

It will be delivered through a partnership involving Save Our River Trust, Ngāti Raukawa, Horowhenua District Council and other local stakeholders. Save Our River Trust will continue to play a governance role, while Horowhenua District Council will lead project delivery.

“By supporting the next phase of this project, we are helping restore a treasured local asset and leave lasting benefits for future generations," Mr Jones says
